284: ### 6.5 Units of work (CQRS handlers), endpoints, and activity diagrams
285: 
286: Each unit is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler"), in `src/QBrainAi.Services/AgentContext/Commands` or `Queries` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.AgentContext.Commands` or `.Queries`), one file per record and handler, registered by `AddCqrsHandlers`. Every surface dispatches the same record through `IDispatcher`: the controller and the MCP tool call `SendAsync` or `QueryAsync`; the typed client, REPL, and plugins reach them over REST. A handler reports a contract error as `Result<T>.Failure(new AgentContextException(code, statusCode, message, details))`; `McpErrorClassifier` maps `AgentContextException` to the problem+json body with that status and `code`. The stateless invocation is not a unit: it is the plugin process RunStatelessInvocation (section 6.6).
287: 
288: Every REST route below exists under `/qbrainai/agent-context` and the alias `/mcpserver/agent-context` (controller `AgentContextController`, `[ApiController]`, workspace required through `X-Workspace-Path`, authenticated by `WorkspaceAuthMiddleware`). MCP tools live in `FwhMcpTools.AgentContext.cs` with `workspacePath` as the first parameter and JSON-string bodies. The typed client is `AgentContextClient : McpClientBase`, exposed as `QBrainAiClient.AgentContext`. The REPL reaches it as `client.AgentContext.<Method>` (added to the `GenericClientPassthrough` allow-list as `AGENTCONTEXT`; mutating methods registered in `ClientMutationPolicy`; YAML validators registered with explicit `payload.params.<key>` paths). PowerShell plugins call `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method client.AgentContext.<Method> -ParamsObject <params>` with `<params>` from the exported builder named in each unit (`McpPluginShim.psm1`). Builder contract, one builder per externally callable unit: `New-McpAgentContext<Verb>Params` takes one parameter per field of the unit's request record, named in PascalCase, typed string as `[string]`, bool as `[bool]`, int as `[int]`, a decimal score as `[string]` holding the exact lexeme, and a list as `[object[]]` of hashtables with the record's camelCase keys; a parameter is mandatory exactly when the record field is required, an omitted optional parameter is left out of the output (the server applies the record's default), and route ids (`packageId`, `responseId`, `relationshipId`, `hvRequestId`) are mandatory `[string]` parameters; the builder returns an ordered hashtable whose keys are the record's camelCase field names in record order with the values unchanged, and never calls the server (`AgentContextBuilders_ParametersMatchRequestRecords_OutputKeysAndValuesExact`, generated over every unit from `docs/context/agent-context-contract.json`). Tool descriptor contract: each externally callable unit has one entry in `lib/tool-descriptors.json` with `name` (the `agent_context_*` name in each unit), `description`, `inputSchema` (the JSON schema of the unit's request record, route ids as required string properties, scores as strings), `method` (the `client.AgentContext.<Method>` REPL method listed in each unit), and `mutates` (true for commands, false for queries); a TypeScript host's adapter runs `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -ParamsFromStdin` with the call's arguments as JSON on stdin (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008), so PowerShell and TypeScript hosts reach the same command (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell.").
289: 
290: Every unit except GetAgentContextStatusQuery, DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, and RunStatelessInvocation (including CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand and GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery) starts with the same two checks, drawn in each diagram: the workspace resolves (otherwise 404 `Workspace required`), and the mode is not `Off` (otherwise 409 `agent_context_disabled`).

908: ### 6.6 Processes (plugin)
909: 
910: #### Process RunStatelessInvocation: run a stateless invocation (plugin process) [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]
911: 
912: - Not a unit of work: the plugin orchestrates the handlers GetAgentContextStatusQuery (status), BuildAgentContextPackageCommand (build), SubmitAgentResponseCommand (submit), and RunDeterministicGradeCommand (deterministic grade) through the REPL.
913: - Trigger: a delivered user request (Phase A processes ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord and OpenTurnFromPromptHook) on a host whose plugin reads `Mode` through GetAgentContextStatusQuery.
914: - PowerShell core: `Invoke-PluginAgentContextInvocation` in `plugin-hook.ps1`, for all nine hosts (the TypeScript hosts through their adapters). Hosts inject the rendered package through their prompt-context mechanism (hook additional context or the host's system-context API).
915: - Output: in `Stateless` mode the model receives only the rendered package and the request, without prior conversation turns; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but not injected; in `Off` nothing happens.
916: - Package failure (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation"): in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode, when the build fails (budget overflow, profile unavailable, commit unavailable, any other error, or an outage), the plugin refuses the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator, produces no answer, and closes the request's turn `canceled` with that reason (canceled turns are not gated, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002). A host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt cannot run `Pilot` or `Stateless`; its plugin treats those modes as `Off` and its feature-matrix row records the limitation.
917: - A host recorded `turn_logging_unsupported` (Phase A, D6) has no minted turn, so RunStatelessInvocation does not run there: the plugin stays stateful and reports `turn_logging_unsupported`.
918: - After the model answers, the response is submitted (SubmitAgentResponseCommand) at turn close and graded deterministically (RunDeterministicGradeCommand); its model grade comes later from an HV request covering its turn (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand).
919: 
920: ```mermaid
921: flowchart TD
922:     S(["Request delivered"]) --> SUP{"Host supported for turn logging and the turn minted?"}
923:     SUP -->|no| UNS(["turn_logging_unsupported: stateful, no package"])
924:     SUP -->|yes| MD["Read Mode from status (cached per host session start)"]
925:     MD --> M{"Mode"}
926:     M -->|Off| OFF(["Stateful turn as today"])
927:     M -->|Pilot or Stateless| CAN{"Host prompt hook can refuse a prompt?"}
928:     CAN -->|no| LIM(["Treated as Off: stateful, limitation in the feature matrix"])
929:     CAN -->|yes| BP["Build package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand) for sessionId and requestId, idempotency key = requestId"]
930:     BP --> BR{"Build result"}
931:     BR -->|any error or outage| REF["Refuse the prompt with the error code and message shown to the operator"]
932:     REF --> CN["Close the turn canceled with the reason"]
933:     CN --> FAIL(["Invocation failed: no answer produced"])
934:     BR -->|built| MM{"Mode"}
935:     MM -->|Pilot| PIL["Record packageId on the turn, no injection"]
936:     PIL --> RUN1["Model answers statefully"]
937:     MM -->|Stateless| INJ["Inject the rendered package as the model context, no history"]
938:     INJ --> RUN2["Model answers from the package"]
939:     RUN1 --> SUB["At turn close submit the response (SubmitAgentResponseCommand) with claims, evidence, and invocationMode"]
940:     RUN2 --> SUB
941:     SUB --> SR{"Submit result"}
942:     SR -->|201 or 200| GRD["Deterministic grade (RunDeterministicGradeCommand)"]
943:     SR -->|error or outage| SE["Record the cause on the turn, keep the turn open for the Stop gate"]
944:     SE --> E3(["Response not recorded: the model or operator resubmits"])
945:     GRD --> GDR{"Grade result"}
946:     GDR -->|201| WAIT(["Response Grading until an HV request covering the turn records its model grade (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand)"])
947:     GDR -->|error| GE(["Cause recorded on the turn: the deterministic grade is re-run on request"])
948: ```

551: ### Use cases (new, 9)
552: 
553: UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001.

555: UC-2 Persist session-log writes with truthful receipts. Actors: model, plugin, server. Basic flow: model calls a verb; plugin persists; server returns per-turn outcome; plugin reports persisted only for created/merged. Alternate: target turn is terminal, server reports `skipped_terminal`, plugin reports `persisted:false`, exits non-zero, clears the failsafe; legacy server without outcomes yields `outcomeVerified:false`. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003, FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001.
556: 
557: UC-3 Close every request turn before stopping. Actors: model, host Stop hook. Basic flow: model records actions/decisions (incl. via `designDecisions`) and closes each turn; Stop hook finds all closed with evidence and passes, clearing the ledger. Alternate: a turn is open (including one whose close the plugin refused for missing model evidence) or its most recent close was refused by the server's completion gate, the Stop hook blocks with the reason and the accepted remedy; a turn closed without evidence by another surface is only warned and never closes turns itself. Alternate: the host session failed closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`) while a turn was open; the Stop hook blocks with the reduced remedy (only the missing model evidence, the missing `requestClass` from S8/S9, and the close call; the terminal reviews are judged at the drain), the model's evidence and close for that turn are captured in the plugin failsafe (reviews are refused and recorded after the drain through the original pair), the next Stop warns instead of blocking, and the next SessionStart drains the captured records with the turn's original pair through the trusted recovery flow. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005, -006; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005, FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001.

Basic flow: model sets `requestClass` (Code, Docs, Chore) on its turn; an `Unstarted` hostile record flips to Unnecessary for Chore (and back if the class changes away while it is still Unnecessary), on in-progress turns only; records past Unstarted are never changed automatically. Alternate: invalid value rejected. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006.

Alternate: gate unmet, 400 with missing items, turn stays in progress; fail requires only class; exempt origins bypass; the plugin, REPL, and McpAgent pre-checks only warn with the exact gate message and never refuse (the server gate is the only authority), and a server refusal is reported with the server's message and missing items; `canceled` is not gated. I want every unit of work request and respone defined.  I want every endpoint defined."); P0.4 creates the records from exactly that completed text, and HV-P0 (P0.9) reviews the created records against it. Each FR gets one TR (implementation ACs, unit names GetAgentContextStatusQuery, BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, GetAgentContextPackageQuery, QueryAgentContextPackagesQuery, ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery, SubmitAgentResponseCommand, GetAgentResponseQuery, QueryAgentResponsesQuery, RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand, DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand, CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand, QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery, RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand, process RunStatelessInvocation, GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery, CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery) and one TEST (three-AC rule), all priority high, area MCP, mapped FR to TR to TEST.
574: 
575: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 Context package construction and provenance: the server builds a bounded, reproducible package for a session-log turn from the request, the canonical profile and rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, records source hashes, commit identity, selection rationale, token usage, contradictions, blockers, and omitted candidates, and replays it identically from its stored input snapshot, never from live sources or configuration (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, GetAgentContextPackageQuery, QueryAgentContextPackagesQuery, ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery).
576: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-002 Token budget and explicit overflow: mandatory context is never truncated; when it exceeds the budget the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`, stores an `Overflow` package for audit, and reports the token counts and mandatory items (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand).
577: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-003 Response submission: an agent response is submitted against a built package with its claims and evidence, idempotently, carrying the package's root ids (SubmitAgentResponseCommand, GetAgentResponseQuery, QueryAgentResponsesQuery).
578: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-004 Grading and trust: every response is graded by deterministic evidence checks and by the configured independent model grader, the latter recorded by the HV agent for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns (no grading worker or HV pipeline in this effort, operator 2026-10-11); a model grade is accepted only from the configured grader, for a response inside an open HV request, with verified jsonl receipts, and only when its scores and findings equal the reviewer's own verdict entry for that response and the reviewer's own session-log turn, from a session independent of the reviewed one, holds that verdict (architecture section 6.3); a response is trusted only when both latest grades reach the trust thresholds, never below 98 percent, with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN (RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand, DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery).
579: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005 Rejection, staleness, and supersession: rejected, stale, and superseded responses are preserved for audit and excluded from trusted retrieval; a response becomes stale when a dependency it was built on changes (RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand).
580: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-006 Typed relationships: packages, responses, requirements, turns, TODOs, code files, receipts, profile, and rules are linked with `implements`, `verifies`, `depends_on`, `supports`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, `blocks`, `derived_from`, and `relevant_to` (CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand, QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery).
581: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-007 GraphRAG projection with deterministic fallback: trusted responses are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval and removed when they stop being trusted; retrieval falls back to a deterministic relational path with a stated reason whenever GraphRAG cannot answer (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand).
582: - FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-008 Surfaces: every externally callable agent-context unit (GetAgentContextStatusQuery, BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, GetAgentContextPackageQuery, QueryAgentContextPackagesQuery, ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery, SubmitAgentResponseCommand, GetAgentResponseQuery, QueryAgentResponsesQuery, RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand, CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand, QueryAgentContextRelationshipsQuery, RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand, GetAgentContextPilotReportQuery, CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery) is available through REST (`/qbrainai/agent-context/*` and the `/mcpserver` alias), MCP tools, the typed client, the REPL (`client.AgentContext.*`), and the plugin builders and tools of all nine plugins; the two internal units have no endpoint by design: DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand (the trust decision, run inside RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand) and process RunStatelessInvocation (the plugin's stateless invocation, run by the plugins' prompt hooks).

273:- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 When the server is unreachable at ingress, the hook persists a failsafe mint record carrying its nonce and opens a provisional local turn `pending-<nonce>`; on failsafe drain the server mints idempotently from the nonce and the plugin rebinds the provisional turn and every write bound to it to the minted requestId, in original order. Either id resolves to the same turn; a crash at any point during the rebind loses no write and creates no second turn; a committed pending-to-minted alias stays discoverable and is reapplied until every consumer of it (including an audit outbox) durably acknowledges it, and duplicate delivery or application is harmless (C2). With two or more consumers, an alias acknowledged by one stays discoverable to the others; replay to a consumer stops only after that consumer durably acknowledges, and stops entirely once all have. No server turn ever has a `pending-` requestId: a write captured under a pending id and sent after the alias is sent under the minted id, and the writes of one turn reach the server in their original order even when a close of that turn was made while earlier writes waited in the failsafe. A mint that the server or REPL does not support is recognized only by the trusted mint adapter (A3, in the PowerShell core) for the exact mint operation, from either an authenticated, bound mint-endpoint response with HTTP 404 and no detail code, or the structured `unknown_method` (GenericClientPassthrough) or `method_not_found` (ReplCommandDispatcher) result for the expected mint verb, as on a server older than A1; it is never inferred from prose, malformed detail metadata, arbitrary 404s, or unrelated operations, keeps the original structured cause, and is classified as a transport outage by that adapter only (never by the generic C9 classifier or the audit outbox in-call retry loop) and handled like one (failsafe retained, turn stays `pending-<nonce>`, retried at a later drain); a mint refused for a final reason (404 with detail code `session_not_open`, 400 validation) reports `turn-open-failed` with the server code, keeps its failsafe record marked final and not retried, invents no requestId, and the stop gate warns naming the prompt. On drain the plugin first replays an idempotent session open for the record's envelope `mcpSessionId` (an outage that spanned SessionStart left that session unopened on the server), then the mint; a `session_not_open` refusal is final only after that session open is confirmed (`OutageSpanningSessionStart_DrainOpensSessionThenMints_NotFinal`). The pending-to-minted lookup entry is permanent for the life of the plugin cache: retiring an alias's consumer-delivery obligation after the last required acknowledgement never removes it, so a reader holding the pending id resolves the minted turn after every acknowledgement and after a restart. After the delivery obligation is retired, `getAlias` still returns the full agreed record with the exact final acknowledgement set, and a repeated acknowledgement is an idempotent no-op. [A3 +A5 +A8]

1677: ### 7.11 Use case: Build a context package for a request [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001, -002]
1678: 
1679: Actors: agent host and plugin, server. Precondition: the request's turn exists (UC-1) and the mode is `Pilot` or `Stateless`. Basic flow: the plugin asks the server to build a package for the request; the server gathers the request, profile, rules, applicable requirements, related turns, TODOs, receipts, trusted prior responses, and code at the current commit, filters secrets and untrusted items, ranks, fills the budget, records provenance, and returns the rendered package. Alternate flows: mandatory context exceeds the budget and the build fails with `agent_context_budget_exceeded`; the same idempotency key returns the same package; the commit is unreadable; replay proves the package is reproducible.
1680: 
1681: ```mermaid
1682: flowchart LR
1683:     HO(["Agent host and plugin"]) --- U(("Build a context package (BuildAgentContextPackageCommand)"))
1684:     SV(["Server"]) --- U
1685:     U -. include .-> I1(("Retrieve candidates (RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery)"))
1686:     U -. include .-> I2(("Record provenance, omissions, findings"))
1687:     E1(("Mandatory over budget: 422, invocation fails")) -. extend .-> U
1688:     E2(("Repeated key: same package")) -. extend .-> U
1689:     E3(("Replay proves determinism (ReplayAgentContextPackageQuery)")) -. extend .-> U
1690: ```

1693: 
1694: Actors: model, plugin, server, hostile reviewer. Basic flow: at turn close the plugin submits the model's response with its claims and evidence; the server runs the deterministic grade; the coordinator runs the slice HV and records the model grade; the server marks the response trusted when both grades pass at 98/98 with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN. Alternate flows: a grade fails and the response stays `Grading` with every failure shown; a grader other than the configured one is refused; the operator rejects the response.

1780: ### 8.2 What each phase delivers
1781: 
1782: - Prerequisites: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, `TestPluginCore`, `TestAgentPlugins`), and the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell.").

1784: - Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every entity with its `McpDbContext` configuration as compiling model seams (the three migrations and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch), every plugin function and tool signature, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. 1873: ### 8.4 Gates
1874: 
1875: - G1 targeted tests through `./build.ps1 Test --test-projects --test-filter`, G2 the unit gate (`./build.ps1 Test`), G3 integration suites, G4 the PowerShell plugin core through `./build.ps1 TestPluginCore`, G5 config and traceability (`./build.ps1 ValidateConfig`, `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability`), G6 the plugin suites (Pester in all nine repos) through `./build.ps1 TestAgentPlugins`.
1876: - Build.Tests is independent of Nuke and runs directly as the infrastructure check when `build/` changes.
1877: - Windows evidence runs natively on PAYTON-LEGION2 through the operator's WSMan route in a worktree of `F:/GitHub/McpServer`; Linux evidence runs natively on LAB-OMARCHY.
1878:

1880: 
1881: - Merge and deploy order: StorageSchema, SessionTurnLogging, TurnReviews without the CompletionGate enforcement change set, ContextPackages, ResponsesAndTrust, ContextGraph, ReplAndAgents; deploy the server (agent context Mode `Off`); merge PluginCorePowerShell, BuildTooling; sync all nine plugins; merge HostPluginAdoption (then `MAINT-LIBSHRETIRE-001`, and once Codex ACKs the 2026-10-12 PowerShell-only CONTRACT entry or the operator resolves it `MAINT-LIBNODERETIRE-001`); merge and deploy the CompletionGate enforcement change set; Documentation; then the integration checks.
1882: - Mode `Pilot` only on the operator's instruction; the pilot report goes to the operator; `Stateless` as a default is a later operator decision.
1883: - Server deploys run through the Nuke `UpdateService` target with operator approval; releases use Octopus only. Rollback: Mode `Off` stops agent-context behavior without a deploy; migrations roll back only through their tested Down.
1884: 
1885: ### 8.6 End-to-end verification
1886: 
1887: - Turn logging and reviews: the live checks of the plan's "End-to-end verification" section.
1888: - Agent context with Mode `Pilot` on LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2: a delivered request builds one package with the request's root ids; replay reports `identical: true`; an over-budget fixture refuses the prompt with `agent_context_budget_exceeded` and closes the turn `canceled`; a submitted response passes the deterministic grade, an HV request covering its turn is created, the HV agent records a passing model grade with verified receipts, and the response becomes `Trusted`; a later package includes it as a prior response; changing a file it depends on makes it `Stale`; with GraphRAG disabled retrieval reports `graphrag_disabled` and answers from the relational path; with GraphRAG enabled the trusted response is projected and a rejected one removed.

1: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
2: # Architecture: Turn Logging, Turn Reviews, and Stateless Agent Context
3: 
4: Status: architecture documentation of the merged plan PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001 (`docs/plans/PLAN-SESSIONTURN-SESSIONREVIEW-001.md`), pending operator approval of the merged plan. Operator directives (2026-10-11, verbatim): "Integrate attached to current plan.", "Reconstruct plan with added requirements", "Also publish the doc to develop", "Outline now, catalog in P0", "No new code until I approve merged plan.", "I want every model defined.  I want every unit of work request and respone defined.  I want every endpoint defined.", and "I want a single, complete activity diagram (mermaid) for every unit of work.  I want sequence diagrams for submitting each request type and processing every response.  I want a md doc describing the who plan as architecture documentation."; for plugins and scripts, "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell.", "This should have already been the standard for plugins.", and "I have not chosen PowerShell for scripting because of Microsoft or Windows. I have chosen it because it is simply the best tool for the job."
5: 
6: This document describes the whole merged plan as architecture: the components, the data each part owns, every unit of work with its request, response, and error contract, one complete activity diagram per unit of work, and sequence diagrams for submitting each request type and processing each response. The plan document remains the authority for slices, gates, tests, and acceptance criteria; the agent-context contracts are specified in `docs/Stateless-Agent-Context-Management.md`, and this document repeats them so it stands alone.
7: 
8: How to read the diagrams:
9: 
10: - Activity diagrams are Mermaid flowcharts read top to bottom. A rounded terminal is a start or an end, a diamond is a decision, a rectangle is an action, and every error exit is drawn and ends in a terminal that names the error code.
11: - Sequence diagrams show who sends what. Each `alt` block lists every response the caller can receive and how the caller processes it.
12: - Three kinds of activity diagram: a unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler") and is labelled by the record's name; a policy is a rule a handler applies (for example CompletionGate); a process is plugin, host, REPL, or build orchestration that calls handlers (for example ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord). All labels are meaningful names (operator: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers.").
13: - Requirement ids in brackets name the functional requirement the unit of work realizes. Ids of the form `FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-*` are reserved for P0, where the agent-context catalog is created.
14: 
15: ## 1. Goals
16: 
17: 1. One user request is exactly one session-log turn, minted by the server when the message arrives, and every write lands on the turn of the request that caused it (Phase A).
18: 2. Every turn carries a request class and two review records (agent and hostile) with lossless decimal scores, a status lifecycle, configurable thresholds, and a server-enforced completion gate (Phase B).
19: 3. Every agent invocation can run stateless: the server builds a bounded, reproducible context package from the profile, rules, requirements, session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and current code, and only responses graded at 98/98 with no FAIL or UNKNOWN become trusted context for later requests (Phase C).
20: 
21: The agent-context scope depends on the turn-logging scope (turns are the unit a package is built for, and session-log turns are evidence) and on the review scope (the thresholds and the 98/98 grading rule). Phases A, B, and C name scope areas; execution runs in four phases across all three (section 8): requirements, interfaces and code stubs, test-driven unit tests with mocks, and implementation by bounded context with parallel coding agents.
22: 
23: ## 2. System context
24: 
25: ```mermaid
26: flowchart LR
27:     subgraph Hosts["Agent hosts"]
28:         CC["Claude Code / Cowork"]
29:         CX["Codex"]
30:         GK["Grok / Grok Bot"]
31:         CP["Copilot"]

33:     end

35:         PS["PowerShell core lib-ps, the only plugin core: hooks, arrival bridge, verbs, failsafe, stop gate, tool descriptors"]
36:     end
37:     subgraph Clients["Clients"]
38:         REPL["qbrain-ai-repl (workflow.* verbs)"]
39:         CL["QBrainAi.Client (typed REST client)"]
40:         AG["McpAgent / QBAgent"]
41:     end
42:     subgraph Server["QBrainAi.Support.Mcp"]
43:         REST["REST controllers /qbrainai/*"]
44:         MCP["MCP tools (stdio and Streamable HTTP)"]
45:         SL["SessionLogService"]

47:         ACX["AgentContext services: builder, grader, retrieval, staleness"]
48:         GR["GraphRAG (optional)"]
49:     end
50:     DB[("Relational store: SQLite, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server")]
51:     CC --> PS
52:     CX --> PS
53:     GK --> PS
54:     CP --> PS
55:     TSH -- "pwsh: plugin-hook.ps1 and Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1" --> PS
56:     PS --> REPL
57:     REPL --> CL

61:     REST --> SL
62:     REST --> ACX

70: 
71: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions
72: 
73: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
74: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
75: - Plugin scripting: PowerShell only (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."). `plugins/core/lib-ps` is the one plugin core for all nine hosts; cline, cline-v2, and opencode keep only the adapter entry file their host API forces, which forwards host events to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1` and tool calls to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1` and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json`; Pester is the only plugin test runner.
76: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
77: - Errors: every REST error is the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body `{ "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "message", "retryable", "details" }` emitted through `McpErrorClassifier` (`SessionLogController.cs` and the agent-context controller); `code` carries the unit's error code (for example `review_status_conflict`, `agent_context_budget_exceeded`), the HTTP status is the one stated per unit (400 validation, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict or disabled, 422 semantic refusal), and MCP tools return `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
78: - Identifiers: every identifier is human-readable and meaningful (operator, 2026-10-11: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers."). Session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record keys derive from the turn and session they belong to (section 6.3): packages `pkg-<requestId>-<nn>`, responses `rsp-<requestId>-<nn>`, grades `grd-<responseId>-<kind>-<nn>`, relationships `rel-<type>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<nn>`, HV requests `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>`. Document labels use the command, query, process, and policy names.
79: - Root ids: every record carries the root ids of its parents (workspace, MCP session, request, and for agent context the package and response).
80: - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a turn field, a context package, or a response; the session-log sanitizer and the agent-context secret filter redact on write and on every read surface.
81: - Process: every slice follows the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips) and ends with a Codex gpt-6-astra max hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.
82: 
83: ## 4. Phase A: correct, independent turn logging
84: 
85: ### 4.1 Components and data
86: 
87: - Server: `SessionLogService.SubmitWithOutcomesAsync` (per-turn outcomes), `ISessionLogService.MintTurnAsync`, `ISessionLogRequestIdMinter`, `ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard`, `SessionLogTurnEntity.IngressNonce` (unique filtered index per MCP session).

89: - TypeScript-host bindings (cline, cline-v2, opencode) in the same PowerShell core, reached through each host's logic-free adapter, which forwards host events to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1` and tool calls to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1` and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json` (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."); `plugins/core/lib-node` receives no new work and is retired.

92:   - `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml`: `writeTarget { requestId, deliveredAtUtc, source }`, `openDelivered [requestId]`, `queue [{ kind, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }]`, `appliedThroughOffset`, `mcpSessionId`, `ledger [...]`, `unsupportedSince { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason }`; every entry carries the root ids; written by one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock`.

99: stateDiagram-v2
100:     [*] --> queued: enqueue (mint)
101:     queued --> delivered: dequeue of head, or remove with absorbed_mid_turn
102:     queued --> withdrawn: remove with another or no reason, or popAll
103:     delivered --> closed: completeTurn or failTurn confirmed by server
104:     withdrawn --> closed: failTurn "withdrawn before delivery" confirmed
105:     closed --> [*]

110: Each unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler"), following `QBrainAi.Cqrs`: a `sealed record` implementing `ICommand<TResult>` or `IQuery<TResult>` and its handler in the same file under `src/QBrainAi.Services/<Area>/Commands` or `Queries`, registered by `AddCqrsHandlers`, returning `Result<TResult>`; controllers and MCP tools dispatch through `IDispatcher.SendAsync` or `QueryAsync` and map failures through `McpErrorClassifier`. Phase A and B handlers delegate to the `ISessionLogService` members the plan names.

115: - Trigger: a user message arrives at a host arrival mechanism (prompt hook, arrival bridge, or host-native adapter). Only hooks and adapters call it; there is no MCP tool, and the plugin wrapper refuses a model-originated call with `mint_requires_host_ingress`.

404:     LK -->|no| CT(["turn-open-contended: no mint"])
405:     LK -->|yes| NN{"Host nonce field present?"}
406:     NN -->|no| NF(["turn-open-failed nonce_source_missing: failsafe diagnostic, no invented nonce"])
407:     NN -->|yes| MN["Mint with the host nonce (MintSessionTurnCommand)"]
408:     MN --> MR{"Mint result"}
409:     MR -->|created| DV["Deliver: write target, openDelivered, ledger entry"]
410:     DV --> OK(["turn-opened"])
411:     MR -->|merged, turn in progress| EQ{"Equal-field host (copilot or classic cline) and a new invocation?"}
412:     EQ -->|yes| FC(["Fail closed: unsupportedSince indistinguishable_arrival"])
413:     EQ -->|no| AO(["turn-already-open: rebind to the same requestId"])
414:     MR -->|merged, turn terminal| TT(["Report storedStatus: not write target, not open, not ledgered"])
415:     MR -->|outage| PD["Open pending-nonce locally, failsafe mint record"]
416:     PD --> PO(["turn-opened pending: drained later (process DrainFailsafe)"])
417:     MR -->|final refusal| FR(["turn-open-failed with the server code"])
418: ```
419: 
420: #### Process BindVerbToTurn: bind a session-log verb to its turn [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007]
421: 
422: - Verbs: `appendActions`, `appendDialog`, `appendDecisions`, `updateTurn`, `completeTurn`, `failTurn`, `setTurnTitle`, and from Phase B `recordReview`.
423: - Request: the verb's payload plus an optional explicit `requestId`, or a trusted recovery pair (`sessionId`, `requestId`).
424: - Response: the resolved target request id and an immutable invocation binding `{ hostSessionKey, keySource, ingressNonce, requestId, boundAtUtc }` stored with the persist and failsafe records; or a refusal code.
425: - Refusal codes: `request_unknown`, `request_ambiguous`, `turn_immutable`, `host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`, `turn_logging_unsupported`; warning `host_session_inferred`.
426: 
427: ```mermaid
428: flowchart TD
429:     S(["Verb invoked"]) --> SY["Sync-PluginArrivalLog up to the transcript length at start"]
430:     SY --> KEY{"Host session key readable from the invocation context?"}
431:     KEY -->|no| PAIR{"Trusted pair sessionId and requestId supplied and verified on the server?"}
432:     PAIR -->|yes| BP["Bind to the pair"]
433:     PAIR -->|no| LIVE{"Live host sessions of this agent in the workspace"}
434:     LIVE -->|none| HU(["Refuse host_session_unknown"])
435:     LIVE -->|more than one| HA(["Refuse host_session_ambiguous"])
436:     LIVE -->|exactly one| INF["Use it: warning host_session_inferred"]
437:     KEY -->|yes| KS["Load sessions/key/turn-state.yaml"]
438:     INF --> KS
439:     KS --> UNS{"unsupportedSince recorded?"}
440:     UNS -->|yes| OPN{"Target is a turn already open when the session failed closed?"}
441:     OPN -->|yes| FS(["Bind and capture the write to the failsafe as unsupported_session"])
442:     OPN -->|no| UL(["Refuse turn_logging_unsupported"])
443:     UNS -->|no| EXP{"Explicit requestId supplied?"}
444:     EXP -->|yes| KN{"Known open turn of this MCP session?"}
445:     KN -->|no| RU(["Refuse request_unknown"])
446:     KN -->|yes| TERM
447:     EXP -->|no| CNT{"Delivered requests open"}
448:     CNT -->|two or more| AMB(["Refuse request_ambiguous naming the open requests"])
449:     CNT -->|none| NT{"Write target set?"}
450:     NT -->|no| RU2(["Refuse request_unknown naming the host session key"])
451:     NT -->|yes, closed| IM(["Refuse turn_immutable naming the write target"])
452:     CNT -->|exactly one| WT["Target = write target"]
453:     WT --> TERM{"Target locally terminal?"}
454:     BP --> TERM
455:     TERM -->|yes, verb not recordReview or class-only| IM2(["Refuse turn_immutable"])
456:     TERM -->|no, or review or class-only update| B(["Binding captured once: proceed to persist (process PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt)"])
457: ```
458: 
459: #### Process PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt: persist a turn write with a truthful receipt (dispatches UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand through the REPL) [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
460: 
461: - Request: a turn upsert (`POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/turn`, `PATCH` or `PUT .../{requestId}`, `POST .../complete` or `.../fail`) built by `New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest` with the binding.
462: - Response (plugin receipt): `persisted` (bool), `code` (`persisted`, `skipped_terminal`, `queued`, or the server error code), `storedStatus`, `reason`; exit code 0 or 1.
463: 
464: ```mermaid
465: flowchart TD
466:     S(["Bound write ready"]) --> SEND["Send upsert through the REPL"]
467:     SEND --> RES{"Result"}
468:     RES -->|transport outage| FQ["Write failsafe record keyed by the bound requestId"]
469:     FQ --> QD(["Receipt persisted false, code queued: degraded persistence, exit 1"])
470:     RES -->|server error| ER{"Error code"}
471:     ER -->|session_turn_completion_gate| GR["Record the server refusal and missing items locally: turn stays in progress"]
472:     GR --> GRE(["Receipt persisted false with the server message and missing items, exit 1"])
473:     ER -->|other| OE(["Receipt persisted false with the server code, exit 1"])
474:     RES -->|turns outcome list| OUT{"Outcome for the bound requestId"}
475:     OUT -->|created or merged| CL{"Close verb?"}
476:     CL -->|yes| RM["Remove from openDelivered and the ledger after the confirmed close"]
477:     CL -->|no| OK
478:     RM --> OK(["Receipt persisted true, code persisted, storedStatus: failsafe cleared, exit 0"])
479:     OUT -->|skipped_terminal| TS["Cache storedStatus as terminal: later verbs refused locally with turn_immutable"]
480:     TS --> SKR(["Receipt persisted false, code skipped_terminal, failsafe cleared, exit 1"])
481: ```
482: 
483: #### Process DrainFailsafe: drain the failsafe [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005]
484: 
485: - Trigger: SessionStart, and the next verb after an outage.
486: - Input: failsafe records in their original order, each with its captured binding and root-id envelope.
487: - Output: minted ids journaled as aliases, writes replayed onto their own turns, records removed only after a confirmed result.
488: 
489: ```mermaid
490: flowchart TD
491:     S(["Drain starts"]) --> NX{"Next record"}
492:     NX -->|none| E(["Drain complete"])
493:     NX -->|record| LB{"Record has a captured binding?"}
494:     LB -->|no, legacy| KEEP["Retain, never auto-replay, warn at Stop"]
495:     KEEP --> NX
496:     LB -->|yes| SO["Replay idempotent session open for the envelope mcpSessionId"]
497:     SO --> SOR{"Session open confirmed?"}
498:     SOR -->|outage| STOP(["Stop drain: records retained"])
499:     SOR -->|yes| KIND{"Record kind"}
500:     KIND -->|mint| MT["Mint with the original nonce (MintSessionTurnCommand)"]
501:     MT --> MTR{"Mint result"}
502:     MTR -->|session_not_open after confirmed open| FIN["Final: turn-open-failed, record removed"]
503:     FIN --> NX
504:     MTR -->|outage| STOP
505:     MTR -->|created or merged| AJ["Journal alias pending-nonce to requestId in aliases.yaml"]
506:     AJ --> RW["Rewrite queued records of that alias to the minted id"]
507:     RW --> RMV["Remove the mint record"]
508:     RMV --> NX
509:     KIND -->|write| AL{"Write under a pending id with a journaled alias?"}
510:     AL -->|yes| SUB["Send under the minted id"]
511:     AL -->|no| SEND["Send under its bound id"]
512:     SUB --> WR{"Write result (process PersistTurnWriteWithReceipt mapping)"}
513:     SEND --> WR
514:     WR -->|outage| STOP
515:     WR -->|persisted, skipped_terminal, or final refusal| DONE["Record removed and outcome reported"]
516:     DONE --> NX
517:     KIND -->|unsupported_session close| TR["Trusted recovery with the original pair"]
518:     TR --> WR
519: ```
520: 
521: #### Process EvaluateStopGate: evaluate the Stop gate [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005]
522: 
523: - Trigger: every host Stop (Claude Code `stop_hook_active`, Grok `stopHookActive`; on cline-v2 and opencode the stop-equivalent `afterRun` or `session.idle`, forwarded by the adapter to the same PowerShell gate).
524: - Output: `{}` (pass) or a block whose text is `session_turn_stop_gate: <n> turn(s) are not closed correctly:` followed by one line per turn `<id> (<code>): <remedy>` and `The stop gate never closes turns for you.`; warnings in either case. The gate never completes or fails a turn.
525: 
526: ```mermaid
527: flowchart TD
528:     S(["Stop event"]) --> AP["Apply pending transcript records up to the transcript length at Stop start"]
529:     AP --> LD["Load this host session's ledger, open list, withdrawn entries, and failsafe"]
530:     LD --> FD["Compute findings with the pure function (no IO)"]
531:     FD --> EACH{"For each turn of this host session"}
532:     EACH --> REF{"Most recent close refused by the server with session_turn_completion_gate?"}
533:     REF -->|yes| B1["Block session_turn_completion_gate: server missing items first"]
534:     REF -->|no| WDR{"Withdrawn and still in progress?"}
535:     WDR -->|yes| B2["Block turn_withdrawn_unclosed: remedy failTurn withdrawn before delivery"]
536:     WDR -->|no| DLV{"Delivered and still in progress?"}
537:     DLV -->|yes| UNS{"Session unsupportedSince and the close is captured in the failsafe?"}
538:     UNS -->|yes| W1["Warn: unsupported session, drained at next SessionStart"]
539:     UNS -->|no| OUTG{"Model close held in the failsafe by an outage?"}
540:     OUTG -->|yes| W2["Warn: degraded persistence, ledger kept until confirmed"]
541:     OUTG -->|no| B3["Block turn_in_progress: accumulated remedy"]
542:     DLV -->|no| QW{"Queued locally but in progress on the server?"}
543:     QW -->|yes| W3["Warn only"]
544:     QW -->|no| CLR["Closed: eligible to clear"]
545:     B1 --> AGG
546:     B2 --> AGG
547:     B3 --> AGG
548:     W1 --> AGG
549:     W2 --> AGG
550:     W3 --> AGG
551:     CLR --> AGG["Add diagnostics: duplicate_delivery_suspected, nonce_source_missing, unbound legacy failsafe, legacy current-turn"]
552:     AGG --> ANY{"Any block finding?"}
553:     ANY -->|yes| FORCED{"Host forces the stop anyway?"}
554:     FORCED -->|yes| OV(["Record stop_gate_overridden_by_host"])
555:     FORCED -->|no| BLK(["Block with the message: re-evaluated on every Stop, including stop_hook_active"])
556:     ANY -->|no| CL2["Clear confirmed-closed ledger entries in one atomic replace"]
557:     CL2 --> PASS(["Pass with {} and any warnings"])
558: ```
559: 
560: #### Process ValidateHookRegistration: validate and repair hook registration [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001]
561: 
562: - Surfaces: `validate-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` (check or repair) and `install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` in the Claude plugin repo.
563: - Output JSON: the validator's existing result plus the new `duplicate` and `repaired` statuses and the fields `duplicateHooks`, `pluginEnabled`, and `pluginKey`. The installer adds no bridge hook for an event the enabled plugin already covers, and removes managed duplicates with a backup.
564: 
565: ```mermaid
566: flowchart TD
567:     S(["Validator runs"]) --> EN["Test-PluginEnabled: read the enabledPlugins map and resolve keys through known_marketplaces.json"]
568:     EN --> INV["Get-DuplicateHookCommands: inventory MCP hook commands in the active settings layers and the enabled plugin"]
569:     INV --> DUP{"Any event registered more than once?"}
570:     DUP -->|no| OK(["Existing result with pluginEnabled and pluginKey"])
571:     DUP -->|yes| CO{"CheckOnly?"}
572:     CO -->|yes| RD(["status duplicate with duplicateHooks: no file changed"])
573:     CO -->|no| BK["Back up settings files"]
574:     BK --> RMV["Remove managed duplicate bridge hooks, keep user hooks"]
575:     RMV --> RV(["status repaired: restart the host"])
576: ```
577: 
578: #### Process StartHostSession: start a host session [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007]
579: 
580: ```mermaid
581: flowchart TD
582:     S(["SessionStart hook"]) --> K["Resolve host session key"]
583:     K --> LK["Take turn-open.lock"]
584:     LK --> MS["Record this host session's mcpSessionId in turn-state.yaml"]
585:     MS --> BR{"Host uses the arrival bridge?"}
586:     BR -->|yes| PID{"Bridge running for this key?"}
587:     PID -->|yes, live pid| SKIP["Keep it"]
588:     PID -->|no or stale pid| START["Start the bridge for this key"]
589:     BR -->|no| SY
590:     SKIP --> SY["Sync-PluginArrivalLog up to the transcript length at start"]
591:     START --> SY
592:     SY --> DR["Drain the failsafe (process DrainFailsafe)"]
593:     DR --> LG{"Legacy current-turn.yaml turn in progress?"}
594:     LG -->|yes| LST["List it: addressable by explicit requestId"]
595:     LG -->|no| OPN
596:     LST --> OPN["List this host session's open turns with their pairs"]
597:     OPN --> CAU{"unsupportedSince cause clearable by its rule?"}
598:     CAU -->|yes| CLR["Clear the cause"]
599:     CAU -->|no| E
600:     CLR --> E(["Session ready"])
601: ```
602: 
603: #### Process EndHostSession: end a host session [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007]
604: 
605: ```mermaid
606: flowchart TD
607:     S(["SessionEnd hook"]) --> W["Write sessions/key/ended.yaml with reason session_end"]
608:     W --> B{"Arrival bridge running for the key?"}
609:     B -->|yes| ST["Stop the bridge"]
610:     B -->|no| E
611:     ST --> E(["Ended: an ended session is never revived"])
612: ```
613: 
614: #### Process SyncAgentPluginsAtVersion: sync the agent plugins at a fixed version [TR-MCP-NUKE-003 under FR-MCP-BUILD-001]
615: 
616: - Surface: `./build.ps1 SyncAgentPlugins --agent-plugin-parent <dir> --plugin-version <x.y.z>` (Nuke), then `./build.ps1 ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly --agent-plugin-parent <dir>`.
617: - Output: a receipt listing exactly nine repos with version and `lib/plugin-hook.ps1` SHA-256; the gate fails on any other count or a mismatch. `ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly` then fails on any bats, bash, Node, or Python script outside each TypeScript host's adapter entry file (TR-MCP-NUKE-003 AC-005).
618: 
619: ```mermaid
620: flowchart TD
621:     S(["SyncAgentPlugins"]) --> PR{"Plugin parent resolves to the nine repos?"}
622:     PR -->|no| F1(["Fail: repos missing"])
623:     PR -->|yes| EACH["For each of the nine repos"]
624:     EACH --> PS["Copy lib-ps and lib/tool-descriptors.json, write CORE-MANIFEST.yaml hashes, run check-core-integrity"]
625:     PS --> KIND{"TypeScript host that loads compiled output?"}
626:     KIND -->|yes| BLD["Compile the adapter with the host's existing build: a build step, never a test"]
627:     BLD --> VER{"Version already the target?"}
628:     KIND -->|no| VER
629:     VER -->|yes| KEEP["Refresh content only: no bump"]
630:     VER -->|no| BUMP["Write the target version: npm version in a TypeScript host, never a lockfile edit"]
631:     KEEP --> MORE{"More repos?"}
632:     BUMP --> MORE
633:     MORE -->|yes| EACH
634:     MORE -->|no| RC["Write the receipt: nine repos, versions, plugin-hook SHA-256"]
635:     RC --> CV{"All nine converged on version and hash?"}
636:     CV -->|no| F3(["Fail the gate: re-run until converged"])
637:     CV -->|yes| PSO{"ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly: no bats, bash, Node, or Python script outside each adapter entry file?"}
638:     PSO -->|no| F4(["Fail: non-PowerShell script found"])
639:     PSO -->|yes| OK(["Sync passes"])
640: ```
641: 
642: 
643: #### Process RunArrivalBridge: arrival bridge lifecycle (claude-code, claude-cowork) [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001]
644: 
645: ```mermaid
646: flowchart TD
647:     S(["SessionStart for a bridge host"]) --> PID{"arrival-bridge.pid for this host session key names a live bridge?"}
648:     PID -->|yes| KEEP(["Keep the running bridge"])
649:     PID -->|no or stale| ST["Start the bridge, write its pid"]
650:     ST --> CUR["Read appliedThroughOffset and the transcript path"]
651:     CUR --> LOOP{"New complete records past the offset?"}
652:     LOOP -->|no| WAIT["Wait for the transcript to grow"]
653:     WAIT --> END1{"SessionEnd marker written?"}
654:     END1 -->|yes| STOP(["Bridge stops"])
655:     END1 -->|no| LOOP
656:     LOOP -->|yes| APPLY["Apply each record (process ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord)"]
657:     APPLY --> FC{"Fail-closed condition recorded?"}
658:     FC -->|yes| UNS(["Bridge stops before the record: unsupported, cursor not advanced"])
659:     FC -->|no| LOOP
660: ```

870:     participant M as Model

872:     participant R as qbrain-ai-repl
873:     participant S as SessionLogController
874:     participant L as SessionLogService

882:         opt items missing

896:             P->>P: remove from openDelivered and the ledger

902:             R-->>P: refusal

906:             S-->>R: skipped_terminal
907:             P-->>M: persisted false, skipped_terminal
908:         else outage
909:             R-->>P: outage
910:             P->>P: failsafe close, ledger kept until confirmed

913:     end

1002: ## 5. Phase B: request class, review records, thresholds
1003: 
1004: ### 5.1 Data model
1005: 
1006: - `SessionLogTurnEntity` gains `RequestClass` (16, indexed) and, per review kind (agent, hostile): `Status` (16, required), `OtherNotes` (text), `Correctness`, `Completeness`, `CorrectnessThreshold`, `CompletenessThreshold` (decimal, precision 29 scale 28), `Reviewer` (256), `ReviewedAt` (UTC), `RequestJsonlPath`, `ResponseJsonlPath` (2048).
1007: - Child `SessionLogTurnReviewReasonEntity { Id, WorkspaceId, SessionLogTurnId, Kind, Ordinal, Value }`.
1008: - Backfill: `RequestClass = Unclassified`, both review statuses `Unstarted`, on every existing row including soft-deleted rows.
1009: - Wire shape on `UnifiedRequestEntryDto`: `requestClass` and the two review objects `agentReview`, `hostileReview` with `status`, `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness`, `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold`, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`; unset fields are emitted as `null`.
1010: - Request classes: `Code`, `Docs`, `Chore` (case-insensitive in, PascalCase out); `Unclassified` exists only for legacy rows.
1011: - Review statuses: `Unnecessary`, `Unstarted`, `Running`, `Pass`, `Fail`, `Other`; `Unnecessary` and `Unstarted` are server-managed, and a review body naming either is refused with `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable` (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC004, case `ReviewController_ClientCannotWriteUnstarted`).
1012: - Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}`, decimal in [0,1], default 0.98, inclusive, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`.
1013: 
1014: ```mermaid
1015: stateDiagram-v2
1016:     [*] --> Unstarted: turn created
1017:     Unstarted --> Unnecessary: hostile only, class set to Chore on an in-progress turn
1018:     Unnecessary --> Unstarted: class changes away from Chore while still Unnecessary
1019:     Unstarted --> Running: review started (reviewer required)
1020:     Unstarted --> Pass: scores meet both thresholds
1021:     Unstarted --> Fail: a score below its threshold
1022:     Unstarted --> Other: otherNotes required
1023:     Running --> Pass
1024:     Running --> Fail
1025:     Running --> Other
1026:     Pass --> Pass: latest write wins
1027:     Pass --> Fail
1028:     Fail --> Pass
1029:     Pass --> Other
1030:     Fail --> Other
1031:     Other --> Pass
1032:     Other --> Fail
1033: ```
1034: 
1035: ### 5.2 Units of work (CQRS handlers)
1036: 
1037: The same rule as section 4.2: each unit is one command or query and its handler. Request classification and the completion gate are not units of their own; they are policies the turn write and close handlers (UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand) apply (section 5.3).
1038: 
1039: #### RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand: record a review [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, -002, -003, -004, -005, -006, -007, FR-SUPPORT-016]
1040: 
1041: - Handler: `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, string RequestId, SessionLogTurnReviewKind Kind, SessionLogTurnReviewInput Review) : ICommand<SessionLogTurnReviewDto>` and `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand.cs`, applying policy HvVerdictMapping when `hvVerdict` is supplied.
1042: - Surfaces: `PUT /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/sections/{section}` with section `agentReview` or `hostileReview` (aliases `agent-review`, `agent_review`, `hostile-review`, `hostile_review`, case-insensitive); MCP `sessionlog_record_review(agent, sessionId, requestId, kind, reviewJson, workspacePath)`; client `RecordTurnReviewAsync`; REPL and plugin `workflow.sessionlog.recordReview` (plugin also accepts `hvReceiptPath`, mapped locally; hostile kind accepts `hvVerdict`).
1043: - Request `SessionLogTurnReviewInput`: `status` (optional), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (JSON number or numeric string, lexeme `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`, at most 28 fractional digits, value in [0,1]), `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC with offset), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`, `hvVerdict` (hostile only). Thresholds on input are ignored.
1044: - Response: the turn's review record with server-derived status and stamped thresholds. Works on every turn status, including completed and failed turns.
1045: - Errors (400 `validation_error` with the code unless noted): `review_invalid_status`, `review_unnecessary_not_client_writable`, `review_other_notes_not_allowed`, `review_other_notes_required`, `review_field_forbidden_for_status`, `review_field_required_for_status`, `review_score_out_of_range`, `review_receipt_paths_required`, `review_score_format`, `review_score_precision`, `review_field_too_long`, `review_timestamp_invalid`, `review_reason_blank`, 422 `review_status_conflict` (includes the thresholds in force and the derived status).
1046: 
1047: ```mermaid
1048: flowchart TD
1049:     S(["Review write received"]) --> SEC{"Section is agentReview or hostileReview or an alias?"}
1050:     SEC -->|no| E0(["400 validation_error unknown section"])
1051:     SEC -->|yes| LEX{"Score lexemes match the pattern, at most 28 fraction digits, value in 0..1?"}
1052:     LEX -->|format| E1(["400 review_score_format"])
1053:     LEX -->|precision| E2(["400 review_score_precision"])
1054:     LEX -->|range| E3(["400 review_score_out_of_range"])
1055:     LEX -->|ok| HV{"Hostile kind with hvVerdict?"}
1056:     HV -->|yes| MAP["Policy HvVerdictMapping: map the verdict to status, reasons, and otherNotes"]
1057:     HV -->|no| ST
1058:     MAP --> ST{"Status supplied?"}
1059:     ST -->|Unnecessary or Unstarted| E4(["400 review_unnecessary_not_client_writable"])
1060:     ST -->|not a known status| E5(["400 review_invalid_status"])
1061:     ST -->|omitted| DER{"Both scores present?"}
1062:     DER -->|no| E6(["400 review_field_required_for_status"])
1063:     DER -->|yes| DRV["Derive Pass or Fail against the thresholds in force"]
1064:     ST -->|Pass or Fail| CMP["Derive from scores against the thresholds in force"]
1065:     CMP --> CF{"Supplied status equals derived?"}
1066:     CF -->|no| E7(["422 review_status_conflict with thresholds and derived status"])
1067:     CF -->|yes| FLD
1068:     ST -->|Running or Other| FLD
1069:     DRV --> FLD{"Per-status fields valid?"}
1070:     FLD -->|forbidden field present| E8(["400 review_field_forbidden_for_status"])
1071:     FLD -->|required field missing| E9(["400 review_field_required_for_status"])
1072:     FLD -->|hostile Pass or Fail without both jsonl paths| E10(["400 review_receipt_paths_required"])
1073:     FLD -->|otherNotes text and status not Other| E11(["400 review_other_notes_not_allowed"])
1074:     FLD -->|Other with blank otherNotes| E12(["400 review_other_notes_required"])
1075:     FLD -->|blank reason| E13(["400 review_reason_blank"])
1076:     FLD -->|timestamp without offset| E14(["400 review_timestamp_invalid"])
1077:     FLD -->|field over its length| E15(["400 review_field_too_long"])
1078:     FLD -->|valid| SAN["Sanitize text fields"]
1079:     SAN --> STAMP["Stamp the thresholds in force"]
1080:     STAMP --> SAVE["Replace the record: latest write wins, any turn status"]
1081:     SAVE --> OK(["200 review record with derived status and stamped thresholds"])
1082: ```

1084: #### ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand: reset a review section [FR-SUPPORT-016, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001]
1085: 
1086: - Handler: `ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId, string RequestId, SessionLogTurnReviewKind Kind) : ICommand<SessionLogTurnReviewDto>` and `ResetSessionTurnReviewCommandHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Commands/ResetSessionTurnReviewCommand.cs`. The item route is not a review unit: it stays on the existing delete-item handler, which refuses review sections.

1092: flowchart TD
1093:     S(["DELETE review section"]) --> IT{"Item key in the route?"}
1094:     IT -->|yes| E1(["400: items cannot be deleted from a review section"])
1095:     IT -->|no| TS{"Turn completed or failed?"}
1096:     TS -->|yes| E2(["400 review_section_reset_on_terminal_turn: nothing changed"])
1097:     TS -->|no| DEF{"Hostile kind and class Chore?"}

1104: #### GetSessionLogQuery: read one session with its turns and reviews [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004]
1105: 
1106: - Handler: `GetSessionLogQuery(string WorkspacePath, string Agent, string SessionId) : IQuery<UnifiedSessionLogDto>` and `GetSessionLogQueryHandler` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/SessionLog/Queries/GetSessionLogQuery.cs`.
1107: - Surfaces: REST `GET /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}` only (the typed client and the REPL have no single-session read; they use QuerySessionLogsQuery with the sessionId filter).
1108: - Response: both review records with exact decimal scores (a 28-digit score reads back byte-equal), sanitized text, and `null` for unset fields.

1120: #### QuerySessionLogsQuery: query sessions and turns with their reviews [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004]

1136: ### 5.3 Policies applied inside handlers
1137: 
1138: #### Policy RequestClassification: request classification and the Chore flip [FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006]
1139: 
1140: - Applied by: UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand whenever a write carries `requestClass` (surfaces: `requestClass` on `updateTurn`, `completeTurn`, `failTurn` through REST turn upsert, PATCH, PUT, complete, fail, MCP tools, client, REPL, and plugin verbs).
1141: - Request: `requestClass` (string). Response: the turn with canonical `requestClass` and the review records after any lifecycle effect.
1142: - Errors: 400 `request_class_invalid`.
1143: 
1144: ```mermaid
1145: flowchart TD
1146:     S(["Write carries requestClass"]) --> N["Normalize case-insensitively"]
1147:     N --> V{"Code, Docs, or Chore?"}
1148:     V -->|no, including Unclassified from an agent surface| E(["400 request_class_invalid: nothing changed"])
1149:     V -->|yes| SET["Store canonical PascalCase class"]
1150:     SET --> IP{"Turn in progress?"}
1151:     IP -->|no| DONE(["Class stored: no review lifecycle change"])
1152:     IP -->|yes| CH{"New class Chore?"}
1153:     CH -->|yes| HU{"Hostile status Unstarted?"}
1154:     HU -->|yes| FL["Hostile becomes Unnecessary"]
1155:     HU -->|no| DONE
1156:     CH -->|no| HN{"Hostile status Unnecessary?"}
1157:     HN -->|yes| BK["Hostile returns to Unstarted"]
1158:     HN -->|no| DONE
1159:     FL --> DONE
1160:     BK --> DONE
1161: ```
1162: 
1163: #### Policy HvVerdictMapping: HV verdict mapping (server) [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005]
1164: 
1165: - Applied by: RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand when a hostile review carries `hvVerdict`, with the thresholds in force at that write.
1166: 
1167: ```mermaid
1168: flowchart TD
1169:     S(["hvVerdict and scores received"]) --> D["Derive Pass or Fail from the scores and the thresholds in force"]
1170:     D --> V{"hvVerdict"}
1171:     V -->|AGREE| R1(["Status = derived Pass or Fail"])
1172:     V -->|DISAGREE| P{"Derived Pass?"}
1173:     P -->|no| R2(["Status Fail"])
1174:     P -->|yes| C{"Receipt names FAIL or UNKNOWN claims?"}
1175:     C -->|yes| R3(["Status Other: otherNotes names those claims"])
1176:     C -->|no| R4(["Status Other: otherNotes gives the verdict-level reason"])
1177: ```
1178: #### Policy CompletionGate: completion gate [FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, -003, -004]
1179: 
1180: - Applied by: every handler that can transition a turn to `completed` or `failed` (SubmitSessionLogCommand submit, UpsertSessionTurnCommand upsert, PatchSessionTurnCommand patch, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand replace, CompleteSessionTurnCommand complete, FailSessionTurnCommand fail), from S10.
1181: - Policy: `completed` needs `requestClass` and `agentReview.status` in Pass, Fail, or Other; for Code and Docs also `hostileReview.status` in Pass, Fail, or Other; for Chore the hostile review is not checked. `failed` needs `requestClass` only. `canceled` is not gated. Only the transition is gated; terminal enrichment is not re-gated.
1182: - Exempt origins: ServerInternal (`AuditedAgentCliClient`, `WorkspacePolicyService`, `QuadBrainOpenAiChatService`), Replication (federation apply), Import (`SessionLogIngestor`, `TranscriptSessionLogPersister`). Gated: Agent (all external surfaces), `QuadBrainInternalToolExecutor`, REPL importRecovery.
1183: - Error: 400 `session_turn_completion_gate`, message token-prefixed and listing the missing items in the order requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview; the whole write is rejected atomically.
1184: 
1185: ```mermaid
1186: flowchart TD
1187:     S(["Write that transitions a turn"]) --> TR{"Transition to completed or failed?"}
1188:     TR -->|no| PASS(["Not gated"])
1189:     TR -->|yes| OR{"Write origin exempt: ServerInternal, Replication, or Import?"}
1190:     OR -->|yes| PASS
1191:     OR -->|no| CLS{"requestClass present and not Unclassified?"}
1192:     CLS -->|no| MISS1["missing: requestClass"]
1193:     CLS -->|yes| TGT{"Target status"}
1194:     TGT -->|failed| OK
1195:     TGT -->|completed| AR{"agentReview Pass, Fail, or Other?"}
1196:     MISS1 --> TGT2{"Target status"}
1197:     TGT2 -->|failed| REJ
1198:     TGT2 -->|completed| AR
1199:     AR -->|no| MISS2["missing: agentReview"]
1200:     AR -->|yes| HC
1201:     MISS2 --> HC{"Class Code or Docs?"}
1202:     HC -->|no, Chore| DEC
1203:     HC -->|yes| HR{"hostileReview Pass, Fail, or Other?"}
1204:     HR -->|no| MISS3["missing: hostileReview"]
1205:     HR -->|yes| DEC
1206:     MISS3 --> DEC{"Any item missing?"}
1207:     DEC -->|no| OK(["Transition applied"])
1208:     DEC -->|yes| REJ["ChangeTracker cleared: nothing saved"]
1209:     REJ --> ERR(["400 session_turn_completion_gate with missing items in order"])
1210: ```
1211: 
1212: ### 5.4 Processes (plugin, REPL, and McpAgent)
1213: 
1214: #### Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview: convert a hostile-validation receipt into a review write (plugin), then policy HvVerdictMapping [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005]
1215: 
1216: - Plugin side (`ConvertFrom-McpHvReceipt` in the PowerShell core, for every host): input the reviewer's JSON receipt and the response jsonl; output a `recordReview` payload with `correctness = accuracy/100`, `completeness = completeness/100` as exact decimals, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, both jsonl paths, and `hvVerdict`.
1217: - Server side: maps `hvVerdict` with the thresholds in force at that write.
1218: 
1219: ```mermaid
1220: flowchart TD
1221:     S(["HV receipt supplied"]) --> VAL{"Receipt valid: scores, verdict, paths, timestamps?"}
1222:     VAL -->|no| E(["Refused before any write with the exact wire-contract code per field"])
1223:     VAL -->|yes| CV["correctness = accuracy/100, completeness = completeness/100 as exact decimals"]
1224:     CV --> AG{"Verdict AGREE?"}
1225:     AG -->|yes| FU{"Any claim FAIL or UNKNOWN?"}
1226:     FU -->|yes| DIS["Send hvVerdict DISAGREE"]
1227:     FU -->|no| AGR["Send hvVerdict AGREE"]
1228:     AG -->|no| DIS
1229:     AGR --> SRV1["Server derives Pass or Fail from the scores"]
1230:     SRV1 --> R1(["Stored Pass or Fail"])
1231:     DIS --> SRV2{"Scores derive Pass?"}
1232:     SRV2 -->|no| R2(["Stored Fail"])
1233:     SRV2 -->|yes| OTH{"Receipt lists FAIL or UNKNOWN claims?"}
1234:     OTH -->|yes| R3(["Stored Other: otherNotes names those claims"])
1235:     OTH -->|no| R4(["Stored Other: otherNotes gives the verdict-level reason"])
1236: ```
1237: 
1238: #### Process ClearSession: clear a session (clear-session coordinator) [TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001 under FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001]
1239: 
1240: - Surfaces: the clear-session coordinator in the PowerShell core (S8), used by all nine plugins (the TypeScript hosts through their adapters, S9), driven by the clear-session skill in all nine plugins.
1241: - Output: per open request turn of the host session, one of: completed, failed with a reason, or left in progress with its exact missing items. No review is ever fabricated.
1242: 
1243: ```mermaid
1244: flowchart TD
1245:     S(["Clear-session run"]) --> EN["Enumerate open request turns of the host session by original sessionId and requestId pair"]
1246:     EN --> NX{"Next turn"}
1247:     NX -->|none| E(["Report: closed turns and turns left in progress with missing items"])
1248:     NX -->|turn| WD{"Withdrawn?"}
1249:     WD -->|yes| RSN1["Reason: withdrawn before delivery"]
1250:     WD -->|no| BL{"blockers section holds a nonblank model-authored entry?"}
1251:     BL -->|yes| RSN2["Reason: first blocker entry"]
1252:     BL -->|no| RDY{"Meets the completion policy and has model evidence?"}
1253:     RDY -->|yes| CT["completeTurn by original pair"]
1254:     CT --> NX
1255:     RDY -->|no| STAY["Leave in progress, report exact missing items"]
1256:     STAY --> NX
1257:     RSN1 --> PRE{"Model evidence present and class set (not missing or Unclassified)?"}
1258:     RSN2 --> PRE
1259:     PRE -->|yes| FT["failTurn by original pair with the reason"]
1260:     FT --> NX
1261:     PRE -->|no| REP["Report queryText, reason, and missing prerequisites in Stop remedy order"]
1262:     REP --> MW["Model writes designDecision then class by the original pair"]
1263:     MW --> RR["Coordinator rerun reads them back"]
1264:     RR --> FT
1265: ```
1266: 
1267: #### Process AdvisoryCompletionPrecheck: advisory completion pre-check (plugins, REPL, McpAgent) [FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004]
1268: 
1269: - Run by: the plugin close verbs (S8, S9), the REPL workflow (S6), and McpAgent (S7) before they dispatch CompleteSessionTurnCommand or FailSessionTurnCommand. It never refuses: the server gate (CompletionGate) is the only authority.
1270: 
1271: ```mermaid
1272: flowchart TD
1273:     S(["Close requested"]) --> RD["Read the turn's class and review statuses (local cache or server)"]
1274:     RD --> POL["Evaluate the golden completion policy (docs/context/session-turn-review-contract.json)"]
1275:     POL --> M{"Items missing?"}
1276:     M -->|no| SEND(["Dispatch the close"])
1277:     M -->|yes| W["Warn with the exact gate message and missing items"]
1278:     W --> SEND2(["Dispatch the close anyway: the server decides"])
1279: ```
1280: 
1281: #### Process PreserveReviewScoreLexemes: lossless review score handling in the REPL [FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-004]
1282: 
1283: - Run by: `IReplJsonNumberNormalizer` inside `ReplCommandDispatcher.NormalizeJsonElement` and `GenericClientPassthrough.NormalizeForJson` (S6).
1284: 
1285: ```mermaid
1286: flowchart TD
1287:     S(["Number token in a REPL payload"]) --> K{"Key is correctness or completeness inside agentReview, hostileReview, or recordReview?"}
1288:     K -->|no| OLD(["Existing handling unchanged"])
1289:     K -->|yes| LX["Read the raw lexeme (JsonElement.GetRawText or the YAML scalar text)"]
1290:     LX --> P{"Matches the score pattern, at most 28 fraction digits, value in 0..1?"}
1291:     P -->|format| E1(["Error review_score_format"])
1292:     P -->|precision| E2(["Error review_score_precision"])
1293:     P -->|range| E3(["Error review_score_out_of_range"])
1294:     P -->|ok| FW(["Forward the lexeme unchanged as a JSON number token"])
1295: ```
1296: ### 5.5 Phase B sequence diagrams
1297: 
1298: #### Sequence: submit RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand and process each response
1299: 
1300: ```mermaid
1301: sequenceDiagram
1302:     autonumber
1303:     participant A as Model or coordinator
1304:     participant P as Plugin recordReview
1305:     participant R as qbrain-ai-repl
1306:     participant S as SessionLogController or sessionlog_record_review

1317:         S->>L: validate, derive, stamp, replace
1318:         alt valid
1319:             S-->>R: 200 record (derived status, stamped thresholds)
1320:             R-->>P: record
1321:             P-->>A: recorded, exact scores echoed
1322:         else 422 review_status_conflict

1324:             P-->>A: conflict surfaced. Resend without status or with the derived one
1325:         else 400 field code

1329:             R-->>P: outage

1331:         end
1332:     end
